A.explanation: The top of X is shallower than the top of Y and has a smaller area, so $F = pA$ is smaller for X, not greater.

B.explanation: Pressure difference is $\rho g h$ where $h$ is cylinder height, and X is taller than Y so its top-to-bottom difference is larger.

C.explanation: Upthrust equals weight of displaced liquid $\rho_{liquid}Vg$, and $V$ is the same for X and Y so upthrust is the same.

D.explanation: Weight is $\rho_{object}Vg$, and with the same $V$ the object of twice the density has twice the weight.

hints: Look at the diagram for the depth of each top surface below the liquid surface and for the top area of tall thin X compared with short wide Y.
Recall that liquid pressure is $p = \rho g h$ and the force on a horizontal face is $F = pA$, while the top-to-bottom pressure difference depends on the vertical height of the cylinder.
Recall what determines upthrust on a fully submerged body: the density of the liquid and the volume displaced, compared with what determines weight: the density of the solid object.
walkthrough: Identify the givens: X and Y are fully submerged in the same liquid, have equal volume $V$, but $\rho_Y = 2\rho_X$. From the diagram X is tall and thin and Y is short and wide.

State the pressure rule: at depth $h$ in liquid of density $\rho$, $p = \rho g h$. The force on the top face is $F_{top} = p_{top}A_{top}$. X has smaller $h_{top}$ and smaller $A_{top}$, so its top force is smaller.
State the difference rule: $p_{bottom} - p_{top} = \rho g H$ where $H$ is the height of the cylinder. Because $H_X > H_Y$, the difference for X is larger.
State Archimedes principle: upthrust $U$ equals weight of displaced liquid, $U = \rho_{liquid} V_{displaced} g$. For full submersion $V_{displaced} = V$.
Compare X and Y: $\rho_{liquid}$, $g$ and $V$ are identical, so $U_X = U_Y$. Object density affects weight $W = \rho_{object}Vg$, so $W_Y = 2W_X$. This is option C
